statement: A top-5 developer publicly halts frontier training >= 30 days, citing safety (developer announcement + independent confirmation; by 2027-12-31)
status_at_phase_end: Not met in 2023. A widely signed open letter called for a 6-month pause on training beyond the then-frontier; no top-5 developer announced a halt. One developer CEO said a next-generation model was not being trained 'for some time', but this was not framed as a safety halt with a defined duration. Conditional-pause commitments appeared in the first published developer safety frameworks.

items.summary: An open letter called on all AI labs to immediately pause, for at least 6 months, training of systems more powerful than the then-frontier model; it gathered tens of thousands of signatures but no top-5 developer adopted the pause.
items.detail: Future of Life Institute, 'Pause Giant AI Experiments: An Open Letter', published 22 March 2023; page shows 31,810 signatures at fetch time (count is current, not as of 2023). Targets 'AI systems more powerful than GPT-4'.

items.summary: Asked about the pause letter, the CEO of a top-5 developer said the firm was not training its next flagship model and would not for some time; framed as a sequencing statement, not a safety halt of defined duration, and not independently confirmed.
items.detail: The Verge, 'OpenAI's CEO confirms the company isn't training GPT-5 and won't for some time' (Sam Altman, MIT event), 2023-04-14. Does not satisfy the resolution rule (no announced safety-cited halt of a frontier run).

items.summary: A top-5 developer published a scaling policy whose safety-level system 'implicitly requires' it to temporarily pause training of more powerful models if scaling outstrips its ability to meet required safety procedures; a conditional commitment, not an actual halt.
items.detail: Anthropic, 'Introducing Anthropic's Responsible Scaling Policy' (AI Safety Levels, ASL). Publication date 2023-09-19 not visible in the extracted text; date from the announcement's known release (treat as approximate).

items.summary: Another top-5 developer published a beta preparedness framework stating it would only continue capabilities-enhancing development if it could reasonably assure safety when a model reaches 'critical' pre-mitigation risk; again a conditional pause trigger, none invoked in-phase.
